text: mid-course test, track three. So, Freya, you are going to talk about an Icelandic festival. Could you begin by telling us a bit about Iceland? Of course. Well, Iceland is a small northern European country in the Atlantic Ocean. We have quite cold weather with snow and ice in winter, but the weather isn't as cold as in Norway or Sweden. Most of the country is still very rural, and there are only a few big towns and one big city. Because there are so many mountains and ice fields, there aren't many places to build houses and towns, so about 80% of Icelanders live in or near the capital city of Reykjavik on the southwest coast. Tell us about Reykjavik. Well, it's a very safe, clean city. Since we have a good bus system and people like walking, there isn't a lot of traffic or pollution. The streets aren't crowded, but that doesn't mean it's boring. Iceland has a long and ancient history, so there are a lot of museums and other interesting places to visit in the city. It's the best place in the world to learn about the Vikings and other northern European culture. Many people come to Reykjavik for the festivals. We have several music festivals, a design festival and my favorite, the book festival. Reading is a very popular activity in Iceland. Perhaps it's because of the long, dark winters, when we have to stay inside a lot of the time. People read a lot anyway, and we often give books as presents. We have a lot of traditional literature, and there are many new Icelandic books every year. In fact, each year, more and more of them are translated into other languages. Since everyone reads and writes so much, and the population is so small, it means that one in ten Icelanders will write a book in their lives. Wow! So, is the festival just for books in the Icelandic language? No. Writers from all over the world come to celebrate books and reading. It's a big international event. The lectures, readings and workshops are in English, and they are all free. There are other sorts of entertainment too, like dancing and parties. It's a great time to meet your favorite writers, taste traditional dishes and have fun. Anyone who loves books should come.
